XCAT to CT: Phantom Grids and the Affine Round Trip

Scan the heart of an XCAT chest, then lay its ground-truth labels exactly onto the reconstructed image, axial and helical.

A simulation has two voxel grids: the phantom grid (the ground truth, here an XCAT 3.0 chest read at 0.4 mm) and the reconstruction grid (a centred stack of axial slices). Organ ROI statistics, segmentation scores and partial-volume fractions all need the map between them. This notebook builds that map with two affines and one resampler, and proves it exact.

The pipeline. Read the export, find and crop the heart, scan the crop twice, and resample the labels onto each reconstruction. Three facts carry the notebook:

  1. The reconstruction grid is always centred on the isocentre (ReconOptions has no off-centre field). To scan a sub-region, crop the phantom so the region sits there.

  2. BS.phantom_to_world_affine(phantom) and BS.recon_to_world_affine(geom, matrix_size) are the two grids' 4 × 4 voxel → world (cm) matrices.

  3. BS.resample_to_recon(phantom, geom, matrix_size; method = :nearest | :linear) carries the ground truth onto the reconstruction grid.

begin
    """A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
    function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
        ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
        Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
        Mke.hidespines!(ax)
        Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
        return ax
    end

    """The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
    function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
        r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
        arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
            Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
            for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
        ]
        return vcat(
            arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
            arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
            arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
            arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
        )
    end

    """A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
    function arrow!(
        ax,
        a,
        b;
        color = COLORS.muted,
        linewidth = 2.5,
        head = 15,
        linestyle = :solid,
    )
        a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
        Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
        t = b - a
        Mke.scatter!(
            ax,
            [b];
            marker = :utriangle,
            markersize = head,
            rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
            color,
            markerspace = :pixel,
        )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
    `subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
    """
    function node!(
        ax,
        c,
        title;
        subtitle = "",
        w = 3.0,
        h = 1.0,
        accent = COLORS.violet,
        fill = COLORS.card,
        textcolor = COLORS.ink,
        subcolor = COLORS.muted,
        titlesize = 19,
        subtitlesize = 15,
        code = false,
    )
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
            color = fill,
            strokecolor = accent,
            strokewidth = 2,
        )
        strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
        Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
        font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
        dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] + dy;
            text = title,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = titlesize,
            font,
            color = textcolor,
        )
        isempty(subtitle) ||
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                c[1] + 0.05,
                c[2] - 0.22 * h;
                text = subtitle,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = subtitlesize,
                color = subcolor,
            )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
    optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
    `labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
    """
    function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
        ax = canvas(position, limits)
        box(key) = nodes[key]
        function port(from, to)
            a, b = box(from), box(to)
            if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # side by side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
                # one above the other
                s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
                return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
            else
                # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            end
        end
        for (from, to) in edges
            p, q = port(from, to)
            if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # straight across or straight down
                arrow!(ax, p, q)
            else
                # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
                mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
                Mke.lines!(
                    ax,
                    Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                    linewidth = 2.5,
                )
                arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
            end
            haskey(labels, from => to) &&
                Mke.text!(
                    ax,
                    (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                    q[2] + 0.12;
                    text = labels[from => to],
                    align = (:center, :bottom),
                    fontsize = 15,
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                )
        end
        for (_, n) in nodes
            node!(
                ax,
                (n[1], n[2]),
                n[3];
                subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
                accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
                w,
                h,
            )
        end
        return ax
    end

    """
    A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
    of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
    of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
    """
    function gantry!(
        ax;
        sid = 5.4,
        sdd = 9.5,
        angles = (90.0,),
        fan_deg = 50.0,
        r_object = 2.0,
        detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
        labels = ("Tube",),
        dark = true,
        object = true,
    )
        ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
        ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
            color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
        )
        for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
            θ = deg2rad(θ)
            s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
            half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
            # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
            edge = Mke.Point2f[
                s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
                for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
            ]
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
                color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
                strokewidth = 0,
            )
            Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                s * 1.18;
                text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 17,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
        object &&
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
                color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
                strokecolor = ink,
                strokewidth = 1.5,
            )
        return ax
    end

    """
    The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
    `limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
    draw into them, then show the figure.
    """
    function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
        fig = Mke.Figure(;
            size,
            backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
            figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
        )
        axes = [
            canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
            for i in eachindex(titles)
        ]
        for i in eachindex(titles)
            Mke.Label(
                fig[2, i],
                titles[i];
                fontsize = 25,
                font = :bold,
                color = COLORS.night_ink,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
            Mke.Label(
                fig[3, i],
                subtitles[i];
                fontsize = 17,
                color = COLORS.night_muted,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
        end
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
        return fig, axes
    end
end;
chest_sketch!

A simplified axial chest, centred at c, s units per cm (about 34 × 23 cm across): the body, the two lungs, the heart (to the patient's left, the viewer's right), the sternum and the spine. dark draws it in the locator band's colours.

"""
A simplified axial chest, centred at `c`, `s` units per cm (about 34 × 23 cm across): the body,
the two lungs, the heart (to the patient's left, the viewer's right), the sternum and the spine.
`dark` draws it in the locator band's colours.
"""
function chest_sketch!(ax; c = (0.0, 0.0), s = 1.0, dark = false)
    p(x, y) = Mke.Point2f(c[1] + s * x, c[2] + s * y)
    oval(cx, cy, rx, ry) = [
        p(cx + rx * cos(t), cy + ry * sin(t))
        for t in range(0, 2π; length = 90)
    ]
    body = dark ? Mke.RGBAf(0.85, 0.74, 0.62, 0.45) : Mke.RGBAf(0.88, 0.8, 0.7, 1.0)
    lung = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper
    bone = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : Mke.RGBf(0.99, 0.97, 0.93)
    edge = dark ? COLORS.night_muted : COLORS.muted

    Mke.poly!(ax, oval(0, 0, 17, 11.5); color = body, strokecolor = edge, strokewidth = 1.5)
    for side in (-1, 1)
        Mke.poly!(ax, oval(side * 9.0, 0.6, 5.8, 8.4); color = lung)
    end
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        oval(2.0, 1.2, 5.0, 4.2);
        color = (COLORS.red, dark ? 0.85 : 0.75),
        strokecolor = edge,
        strokewidth = 1,
    )
    Mke.poly!(ax, oval(0, 9.7, 2.4, 0.9); color = bone, strokecolor = edge, strokewidth = 1)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        oval(0, -8.0, 2.2, 2.0);
        color = bone,
        strokecolor = edge,
        strokewidth = 1,
    )
    return ax
end
grid!

A regular grid of n = (nx, ny) cells of pitch, centred at c, drawn in color.

"""A regular grid of `n = (nx, ny)` cells of `pitch`, centred at `c`, drawn in `color`."""
function grid!(ax, c, n, pitch; color = COLORS.violet, linewidth = 1.2)
    x0 = c[1] - n[1] * pitch / 2
    y0 = c[2] - n[2] * pitch / 2
    for i in 0:n[1]
        x = x0 + i * pitch
        Mke.lines!(ax, [x, x], [y0, y0 + n[2] * pitch]; color, linewidth)
    end
    for j in 0:n[2]
        y = y0 + j * pitch
        Mke.lines!(ax, [x0, x0 + n[1] * pitch], [y, y]; color, linewidth)
    end
    return ax
end

1. Load the XCAT Phantom

Locate the Export

An XCAT 3.0 chest export (adult male, 50th percentile, with coronary plaque): one 8-bit activity volume, *_act_1.raw, its dimensions in its file name, beside a Material_Spreadsheets/ folder with one material table per contrast state. The data is licensed and not in the repository: the notebook looks in BASISSIM_XCAT_DIR (or docs/notebooks/data/xcat/), and without it every compute cell skips and says so.

const XCAT_DIR = get(ENV, "BASISSIM_XCAT_DIR", joinpath(@__DIR__, "data", "xcat"));
const CONTRAST_STATE = "high_contrast"; # the sheets: non_contrast, low_contrast, high_contrast
find_xcat_export 
find_xcat_export(dir, state) -> NamedTuple or String

The one *act_1.raw in dir, its dimensions read off its name (…_1600x1400x867_…), its anatomy (vmale_50) and the material sheet of contrast state, or a String saying what is missing.

"""
    find_xcat_export(dir, state) -> NamedTuple or String

The one `*act_1.raw` in `dir`, its dimensions read off its name (`…_1600x1400x867_…`), its
anatomy (`vmale_50`) and the material sheet of contrast `state`, or a String saying what is
missing.
"""
function find_xcat_export(dir, state)
    isdir(dir) || return "no XCAT directory (set `BASISSIM_XCAT_DIR`)"
    raws = [f for f in readdir(dir) if endswith(f, "act_1.raw")]
    length(raws) ==
        1 || return "expected one *act_1.raw in the XCAT directory, found $(length(raws))"
    name = only(raws)
    m = match(r"(\d{3,4})[x_](\d{3,4})[x_](\d{3,4})", name)
    a = match(r"^(v(?:fe)?male_\d+)", name)
    (
        m === nothing || a === nothing
    ) && return "cannot read the dimensions or anatomy from $(name)"
    dims = Tuple(parse.(Int, m.captures))
    raw = joinpath(dir, name)
    filesize(raw) == prod(dims) || return "$(name) is not $(join(dims, " × ")) bytes"
    sheet_name = "$(a.captures[1])_materials_heart_$(state).xlsx"
    sheet = joinpath(dir, "Material_Spreadsheets", sheet_name)
    isfile(sheet) || return "no Material_Spreadsheets/$(sheet_name)"
    return (; raw, name, dims, anatomy = a.captures[1], sheet, sheet_name)
end
xcat = find_xcat_export(XCAT_DIR, CONTRAST_STATE);
const HAS_XCAT = xcat isa NamedTuple;

XCAT export: vmale_50_raw_1600x1400x867_8bit_little_endian_act_1.raw (1600 × 1400 × 867 voxels, 1.81 GiB) · materials: vmale_50_materials_heart_high_contrast.xlsx

Read the Mask at 0.4 mm

The export is 0.2 mm isotropic, label 0 is air, and the file runs anterior → posterior along its second axis. Reversing that axis makes y point to the patient's front, so every image drawn with y up has the sternum at the top and the patient's left on the viewer's right. A label-preserving nearest-neighbour step of 2 then reads it at 0.4 mm: still about as fine as the reconstruction pixels below.

read_xcat_mask

The activity volume, y towards anterior (the file runs posterior along axis 2).

"""The activity volume, `y` towards anterior (the file runs posterior along axis 2)."""
read_xcat_mask(raw, dims) = reverse(read!(raw, Array{UInt8}(undef, dims...)); dims = 2)
downsample_labeled

Nearest-neighbour 3D downsample by an integer factor: keeps labels intact.

"""Nearest-neighbour 3D downsample by an integer factor: keeps labels intact."""
function downsample_labeled(phantom::AbstractArray{T, 3}, factor::Int) where {T}
    factor == 1 && return phantom
    nx, ny, nz = size(phantom) .÷ factor
    out = similar(phantom, (nx, ny, nz))
    @inbounds for k in 1:nz, j in 1:ny, i in 1:nx
        out[i, j, k] = phantom[
            (i - 1) * factor + factor ÷ 2 + 1,
            (j - 1) * factor + factor ÷ 2 + 1,
            (k - 1) * factor + factor ÷ 2 + 1,
        ]
    end
    return out
end
const DOWNSAMPLE_FACTOR = 2;
const VOXEL_SIZE_CM = ntuple(_ -> 0.02 * DOWNSAMPLE_FACTOR, 3); # 0.2 mm export × factor
phantom_full_uhr = HAS_XCAT ?
    downsample_labeled(read_xcat_mask(xcat.raw, xcat.dims), DOWNSAMPLE_FACTOR) :
    nothing;

Phantom read: 800 × 700 × 433 voxels of 0.4 mm (231.2 MiB as UInt8), 32.0 × 28.0 × 17.3 cm, 56 labels present.

Materials from the XCAT Sheet

Each sheet row is one organ: a name, its elemental mass fractions (one column per atomic number), its density and its label (Organ ID). Every row becomes an XrayAttenuation.Material keyed by its label; a label the sheet does not name stays air, as Phantom assigns it. The high_contrast sheet puts iodinated blood in the cardiac chambers, the aorta and the coronaries. The table is read before cropping because the organ names are how the heart is found.

import XLSX
const _ATOMIC_MASSES = Dict(
    1 => 1.008,
    6 => 12.011,
    7 => 14.007,
    8 => 15.999,
    11 => 22.99,
    12 => 24.305,
    15 => 30.974,
    16 => 32.06,
    17 => 35.45,
    19 => 39.098,
    20 => 40.078,
    26 => 55.845,
    53 => 126.904,
);
const _I_VALUES_EV = Dict(
    1 => 19.2,
    6 => 81.0,
    7 => 82.0,
    8 => 95.0,
    11 => 149.0,
    12 => 156.0,
    15 => 173.0,
    16 => 180.0,
    17 => 174.0,
    19 => 190.0,
    20 => 191.0,
    26 => 286.0,
    53 => 491.0,
);
compute_ZA_ratio

⟨Z/A⟩ of a composition (mass fractions).

"""⟨Z/A⟩ of a composition (mass fractions)."""
compute_ZA_ratio(comp::Dict{Int, Float64}) = sum(
    w * Z / _ATOMIC_MASSES[Z]
    for (Z, w) in comp
) /
    sum(values(comp))
compute_mean_excitation_energy

Bragg additivity for the mean excitation energy of a composition.

"""Bragg additivity for the mean excitation energy of a composition."""
function compute_mean_excitation_energy(comp::Dict{Int, Float64})
    num = sum(w * Z / _ATOMIC_MASSES[Z] * log(_I_VALUES_EV[Z]) for (Z, w) in comp)
    den = sum(w * Z / _ATOMIC_MASSES[Z] for (Z, w) in comp)
    return exp(num / den) * u"eV"
end
load_xcat_materials 
load_xcat_materials(sheet) -> Dict{Int, XA.Material}

Name | <Z> … | Density | Organ ID → one material per label.

"""
    load_xcat_materials(sheet) -> Dict{Int, XA.Material}

`Name | <Z> … | Density | Organ ID` → one material per label.
"""
function load_xcat_materials(sheet)
    wb = XLSX.readxlsx(sheet)
    data = wb[first(XLSX.sheetnames(wb))][:]
    ncol = size(data, 2)
    (string(data[1, ncol - 1]) == "Density" && string(data[1, ncol]) == "Organ ID") ||
        error("unexpected sheet layout: $(join(string.(data[1, :]), " | "))")
    zcols = [(c, parse(Int, string(data[1, c]))) for c in 2:(ncol - 2)]
    out = Dict{Int, BS.XA.Material}()
    for r in 2:size(data, 1)
        data[r, ncol] isa Number || continue
        comp = Dict{Int, Float64}(
            Z => Float64(data[r, c])
            for (c, Z) in zcols
            if data[r, c] isa Number && data[r, c] > 0
        )
        isapprox(sum(values(comp)), 1; atol = 1.0e-3) ||
            error("mass fractions of $(data[r, 1]) do not sum to 1")
        out[Int(data[r, ncol])] = BS.XA.Material(
            string(data[r, 1]),
            compute_ZA_ratio(comp),
            compute_mean_excitation_energy(comp),
            Float64(data[r, ncol - 1]) * u"g/cm^3",
            comp,
        )
    end
    return out
end
materials_full = HAS_XCAT ? load_xcat_materials(xcat.sheet) : nothing;
# one colour per label ID in every map
const LABEL_RANGE = (0, materials_full === nothing ? 1 : maximum(keys(materials_full)));

61 materials in vmale_50_materials_heart_high_contrast.xlsx; 56 labels present in the volume; labels present but not named by the sheet (read as air): none.

2. Find and Crop the Heart

The heart is found by name: the myocardium (myo…) and blood pools (bldpl…) of the four chambers, the pericardium, the coronary arteries and veins with their walls, and the plaque components (rca…, lcx…, lad…). The aorta is left out: it runs the length of the chest and would stretch the box to the whole export. The bounding box of those labels, padded by 1 cm, is the region scanned. (For a phantom named differently, list the label IDs instead.)

heart_label_ids = materials_full === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        pattern = r"^(myo|bldpl)|pericardium|coronary|^(rca|lcx|lad)\d"i
        sort(
            UInt8[UInt8(id) for (id, mat) in materials_full if occursin(pattern, mat.name)]
        )
    end;

34 cardiac labels: 15 myoLV · 16 myoRV · 17 myoLA · 18 myoRA · 19 bldplLV · 20 bldplRV · 21 bldplLA · 22 bldplRA · 26 coronary_artery · 27 coronary_vein · 29 pericardium · 30 coronary_artery_vessel_wall · 33 coronary_wall_intima · 34 coronary_wall_adventitia · 40 rca1_lipid · 41 rca2_lipid · 44 lad2_lipid · 45 lad3_lipid · 46 rca1_calc · 47 rca2_calc · 50 lad2_calc · 51 lad3_calc · 52 rca1_fib_mat · 53 rca2_fib_mat · 56 lad2_fib_mat · 57 lad3_fib_mat · 58 rca1_adventitia · 59 rca2_adventitia · 62 lad2_adventitia · 63 lad3_adventitia · 64 rca1_intima · 65 rca2_intima · 68 lad2_intima · 69 lad3_intima

heart_bbox = (phantom_full_uhr === nothing || heart_label_ids === nothing) ?
    nothing :
    let
        is_heart = falses(256)
        for id in heart_label_ids
            is_heart[Int(id) + 1] = true
        end
        nx, ny, nz = size(phantom_full_uhr)
        lo, hi = [nx + 1, ny + 1, nz + 1], [0, 0, 0]
        @inbounds for k in 1:nz, j in 1:ny, i in 1:nx
            if is_heart[Int(phantom_full_uhr[i, j, k]) + 1]
                lo .= min.(lo, (i, j, k))
                hi .= max.(hi, (i, j, k))
            end
        end
        hi[1] == 0 && error("no cardiac voxels in the phantom")
        pad = round.(Int, 1.0 ./ VOXEL_SIZE_CM) # 1 cm
        lo .= max.(1, lo .- pad)
        hi .= min.((nx, ny, nz), hi .+ pad)
        (i_lo = lo[1], i_hi = hi[1], j_lo = lo[2], j_hi = hi[2], k_lo = lo[3], k_hi = hi[3])
    end;

Crop the Phantom

An index operation on the mask. The cropped block is all simulate! sees, so nothing outside it is ray-traced or held in device memory. It also changes the object: the rest of the chest is no longer in the beam, so this is a scan of the cardiac block, not of a chest with a small display field. (For that, keep the whole phantom and set a small ReconOptions(fov_cm = …).)

phantom_cropped = heart_bbox === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let b = heart_bbox
        phantom_full_uhr[b.i_lo:b.i_hi, b.j_lo:b.j_hi, b.k_lo:b.k_hi]
    end;

Crop: 373 × 331 × 342 voxels, 14.9 × 13.2 × 13.7 cm · 17.4 % of the 242.5 M-voxel phantom

3. Two Grids, Two Affines

The Phantom and Its Affine

Without an origin, Phantom centres the block on the isocentre (origin = -extent/2 + voxel/2), exactly where the centred reconstruction grid will look. Two phantoms are built from the same crop: phantom_cpu keeps the XCAT labels, for the resampling, and the simulation phantom is compact_materials(phantom_cpu) on the device, the same attenuation with the labels renumbered densely (the sheet's IDs are sparse).

phantom_cpu = phantom_cropped === nothing ?
    nothing :
    BS.Phantom(phantom_cropped, materials_full, VOXEL_SIZE_CM);
phantom = phantom_cpu === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let c = BS.compact_materials(phantom_cpu)
        BS.Phantom(to_gpu(c.mask), c.materials, c.voxel_size, c.origin, c.extent)
    end;

phantom_to_world_affine maps a 0-indexed phantom voxel $(i, j, k)$ to world coordinates in cm, with $v$ the voxel size and $o$ the world position of voxel $(0, 0, 0)$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} v_x & 0 & 0 & o_x \\ 0 & v_y & 0 & o_y \\ 0 & 0 & v_z & o_z \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} i \\ j \\ k \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

A_phantom = phantom_to_world_affine(phantom_cpu) (cm)

Scanner, Protocol and a Tight Reconstruction Grid

The GE Revolution Apex Elite of notebook 01, REVOLUTION_APEX (256 × 0.625 mm rows, a curved Gemstone detector, the large-body bowtie). The grid mapping does not depend on the detector, so any scanner would do. The protocol is an axial cardiac CTA: 120 kVp, 250 mA, a 1 s rotation of 500 views and 5 mm of collimation, each view integrated while the gantry turns (view_samples = 5, notebook 01).

The reconstruction grid is a 14 cm × 14 cm field on 384 × 384 pixels (0.365 mm), eight 0.625 mm slices over the 5 mm beam. It is centred on the isocentre, where the block sits, and it is deliberately smaller than the block in x: a reconstruction grid need not contain the object.

recon_opts = BS.ReconOptions(
    matrix_size = (384, 384, round(Int, protocol.collimation_mm / 0.625)),
    fov_cm = 14.0,
    z_cm = protocol.collimation_mm / 10,
);

The Reconstruction Grid's Affine

The reconstruction grid can be inspected before anything is simulated: CTGeometry is built from the scanner, the protocol and the grid, as the workspace builds it. Its affine has the phantom's form, with the pixel size fov / matrix_size and the centred origin -fov/2 + pixel/2.

geom_inspect = BS.CTGeometry(
    scanner;
    n_angles = protocol.views,
    fov_cm = recon_opts.fov_cm,
    z_cm = recon_opts.z_cm,
    collimation_mm = protocol.collimation_mm,
);

4. Scan A: Axial

The chain of notebook 01: create_workspace → simulate!, then the knobless water beam-hardening correction → FDK → HU with the correction's own μ_water.

sim = phantom === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, sim_opts, recon_opts, phantom)
        t = @elapsed result = BS.simulate!(ws, phantom, protocol, sim_opts)
        out = (sino = Array(ws.sinogram), geom = ws.geom, dose = result.dose, t = t)
        ws = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        out
    end;
bhc = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    BS.calibrate_bhc_water(sim_opts, protocol; scanner, geom = sim.geom);
recon_HU = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        sino = BS.apply_bhc_water(to_gpu(sim.sino), bhc)
        ws = BS.create_fdk_recon_workspace(
            sino,
            sim.geom,
            recon_opts.matrix_size;
            filter = :standard,
        )
        μ = Array(BS.reconstruct!(ws, sino, sim.geom))
        ws = nothing
        sino = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(μ; μ_water = bhc.μ_water_ref))
    end;

5. Labels on the Reconstruction

resample_to_recon takes each reconstruction pixel's world coordinate from A_recon, maps it to a continuous phantom index through inv(A_phantom), and samples the phantom there:

methodoutputuse it for
:nearestUInt8 labelsROI extraction, segmentation scoring
:linearFloat32 (trilinear)continuous fields, and the coverage fraction of one binary mask

Trilinear interpolation of a multi-label mask averages label IDs, which means nothing; for a partial-volume fraction, resample a 0/1 mask of the structure instead.

gt_resampled_nn = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    BS.resample_to_recon(phantom_cpu, sim.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size; method = :nearest);
cardiac_coverage

Fraction of each reconstruction voxel covered by the cardiac labels (trilinear on a 0/1 mask).

"""Fraction of each reconstruction voxel covered by the cardiac labels (trilinear on a 0/1 mask)."""
function cardiac_coverage(mask, geom, matrix_size)
    binary = zeros(UInt8, size(mask))
    for id in heart_label_ids
        binary[mask .== id] .= 0x01
    end
    ph = BS.Phantom(
        binary,
        Dict(0 => BS.XA.Materials.air, 1 => BS.XA.Materials.water),
        VOXEL_SIZE_CM,
    )
    return BS.resample_to_recon(ph, geom, matrix_size; method = :linear)
end
cardiac_coverage_lin = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    cardiac_coverage(phantom_cropped, sim.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size);

gt_resampled_nn is UInt8 384 × 384 × 8, cardiac_coverage_lin is Float32 384 × 384 × 8, recon_HU is Float32 384 × 384 × 8: index (i, j, k) is the same physical voxel in all three.

The Overlay

The central slice, all four panels on the reconstruction grid: the HU image, every label (:nearest), the cardiac labels over the image, and the cardiac coverage fraction (:linear on a 0/1 mask) over the image.

Organ ROI Statistics

With the labels on the reconstruction grid, an organ ROI is one comparison, recon_HU[gt_resampled_nn .== label]. Each label with enough pixels on the central slice is eroded in-plane by one pixel (dropping the partial-volume rim), and its mean HU is compared with the monoenergetic HU of its sheet material at the BHC reference energy. Soft tissue, fat, lung and blood land within a few tens of HU; bone reads low (the single-kVp beam-hardening residual of notebook 01), and thin structures pick up partial volume across the 0.625 mm slice.

roi_stats = recon_HU === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let lab = gt_resampled_nn, k = size(recon_HU, 3) ÷ 2 + 1
        nx, ny = size(lab, 1), size(lab, 2)
        refE, μw = bhc.reference_energy_keV, bhc.μ_water_ref
        # pixels inside the reconstruction circle only
        inside(i, j) = (i - (nx + 1) / 2)^2 + (j - (ny + 1) / 2)^2 <=
            (min(nx, ny) / 2 - 2)^2
        interior(i, j, id) = inside(i, j) &&
            all(lab[i + di, j + dj, k] == id for di in -1:1, dj in -1:1)
        stats = NamedTuple[]
        for id in sort(unique(lab[:, :, k]))
            haskey(materials_full, Int(id)) || continue
            vox = [
                recon_HU[i, j, k]
                for j in 2:(ny - 1), i in 2:(nx - 1)
                if interior(i, j, id)
            ]
            length(vox) < 200 && continue
            mat = materials_full[Int(id)]
            theory = 1000 * (BS.compute_μ_at_energy(mat, refE) - μw) / μw
            push!(
                stats,
                (
                    id = Int(id),
                    name = mat.name,
                    n = length(vox),
                    mean = mean(vox),
                    std = std(vox),
                    theory = theory,
                ),
            )
        end
        (slice = k, energy = refE, rows = stats)
    end;

<details><summary><strong>Bring your own interpolator</strong></summary>

For a B-spline, a sinc kernel or a learned upsampler, compose the two affines yourself: M = inv(A_phantom) * A_recon takes a 0-indexed reconstruction voxel (i, j, k, 1) to a continuous phantom index, which any interpolator (Interpolations.jl, ImageTransformations.jl, your own kernel) can sample:

for k in 0:(nz - 1), j in 0:(ny - 1), i in 0:(nx - 1)
    p = M * [i, j, k, 1.0] # continuous phantom index
    out[i + 1, j + 1, k + 1] = my_interpolator(phantom.mask, p[1], p[2], p[3])
end

The matrix for this scan is below. </details>

6. Scan B: Helical

The same phantom and the same three calls, now with a taller crop scanned by a helical acquisition and reconstructed into 64 axial slices to scroll through. The helical grid has its own affine (a longer z extent than Scan A), and resample_to_recon lands the labels on every slice unchanged.

The crop is Scan A's in-plane box, extended 4 cm beyond the cardiac extent at each end in z (where the phantom allows), so the helix has anatomy to sweep through.

    let b = heart_bbox

        merge(

                k_hi = min(size(phantom_full_uhr, 3), b.k_hi + extra),
            ),
        )

    let b = heart_bbox_tall
        phantom_full_uhr[b.i_lo:b.i_hi, b.j_lo:b.j_hi, b.k_lo:b.k_hi]

phantom_helical_cpu = phantom_cropped_tall === nothing ?
    nothing :

phantom_helical = phantom_helical_cpu === nothing ?

    let c = BS.compact_materials(phantom_helical_cpu)
        BS.Phantom(to_gpu(c.mask), c.materials, c.voxel_size, c.origin, c.extent)

    matrix_size = (384, 384, 64), # 64 slices of 0.625 mm
    fov_cm = 14.0,

The Helical Acquisition

pitch and n_rotations make the protocol helical: 10 mm of collimation at pitch 1.0 over 8 rotations is 8 cm of table travel, centred on the isocentre. The geometry becomes a z-ramped trajectory that :dd_fast projects unchanged (each sub-view of the view integration advanced along z by its share of the table feed), and reconstruct! recognises the helical geometry and runs rebinned weighted FBP. The reconstruction grid is still a centred stack of axial slices, so the affines apply as before.

protocol_helical = BS.CTProtocol(
    kVp = 120,
    mA = 250.0,
    views = 500,
    rotation_time = 1.0,
    collimation_mm = 10.0,
    additional_filters = [("Al", 4.5)],
    pitch = 1.0,
    n_rotations = 8,
);
sim_helical = phantom_helical === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        ws = BS.create_workspace(
            scanner,
            protocol_helical,
            sim_opts,
            recon_opts_helical,
            phantom_helical,
        )
        t = @elapsed result = BS.simulate!(ws, phantom_helical, protocol_helical, sim_opts)
        out = (sino = Array(ws.sinogram), geom = ws.geom, dose = result.dose, t = t)
        ws = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        out
    end;
recon_HU_helical = sim_helical === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        bhc_h = BS.calibrate_bhc_water(
            sim_opts,
            protocol_helical;
            scanner,
            geom = sim_helical.geom,
        )
        sino = BS.apply_bhc_water(to_gpu(sim_helical.sino), bhc_h)
        ws = BS.create_fdk_recon_workspace(
            sino,
            sim_helical.geom,
            recon_opts_helical.matrix_size;
            filter = :standard,
        )
        # helical geometry → rebinned WFBP
        μ = Array(BS.reconstruct!(ws, sino, sim_helical.geom))
        ws = nothing
        sino = nothing
        GC.gc(true)
        Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(μ; μ_water = bhc_h.μ_water_ref))
    end;

7. The Mapping Is Exact

Three checks, for the axial and the helical geometry:

  1. The affine is the reconstructor's grid. The FDK and WFBP back-projectors place reconstruction voxel idx (1-indexed) at world -fov/2 + (idx − ½)·fov/n, the rule recon_to_world_affine encodes; the table gives the largest difference.

  2. The round trip is the identity. A⁻¹ · A · v = v to floating-point precision.

  3. The image is registered to the map. Edges of the reconstruction are correlated with the label boundaries over integer in-plane shifts; the best shift should be (0, 0). A half-voxel or rebinning offset between the forward projector and the back-projector would show here and nowhere else. (A systematic shift below half a pixel also reads (0, 0).)

is_helical(geom) switches the back-projection algorithm, never the grid, so the helical mapping is as exact as the axial one. Softness at a boundary is :nearest quantisation or the reconstruction's point-spread function, not the mapping.

affine_audit = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        # the affine's world coordinate vs the back-projector's voxel-centre rule, and A⁻¹·A·v − v
        function audit(name, geom, ms)
            A = BS.recon_to_world_affine(geom, ms)
            Ainv = inv(A)
            grid_err = 0.0
            rt_err = 0.0
            for ax in 1:3, idx in (1, (ms[ax] + 1) ÷ 2, ms[ax])
                v = zeros(4)
                v[4] = 1.0
                v[ax] = idx - 1
                world_bp = -geom.fov[ax] / 2 + (idx - 0.5) * geom.fov[ax] / ms[ax]
                grid_err = max(grid_err, abs((A * v)[ax] - world_bp))
                rt_err = max(rt_err, abs((Ainv * (A * v))[ax] - (idx - 1)))
            end
            return (name = name, grid_um = grid_err * 1.0e4, roundtrip = rt_err)
        end
        out = [audit("axial", sim.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size)]
        sim_helical === nothing ||
            push!(out, audit("helical", sim_helical.geom, recon_opts_helical.matrix_size))
        out
    end;

registration = sim === nothing ?
    nothing :
    let
        # Correlate reconstruction edge strength with the label-boundary map over integer
        # (dx, dy) shifts on the central slice; the best shift is the real in-plane offset.
        function reg_offset(name, recon, gt; R = 5)
            mid = size(recon, 3) ÷ 2
            hu = Float32.(recon[:, :, mid])
            lab = gt[:, :, mid]
            nx, ny = size(hu)
            gr = zeros(Float32, nx, ny)
            lb = zeros(Float32, nx, ny)
            for j in 2:(ny - 1), i in 2:(nx - 1)
                gr[i, j] = hypot(hu[i + 1, j] - hu[i - 1, j], hu[i, j + 1] - hu[i, j - 1])
                # a symmetric boundary marker (both sides of an edge): no half-voxel bias
                boundary = lab[i, j] != lab[i + 1, j] ||
                    lab[i, j] != lab[i - 1, j] ||
                    lab[i, j] != lab[i, j + 1] ||
                    lab[i, j] != lab[i, j - 1]
                boundary && (lb[i, j] = 1.0f0)
            end
            scores = Dict(
                (dx, dy) => sum(
                    gr[i, j] * lb[i + dx, j + dy]
                    for j in (1 + R):(ny - R), i in (1 + R):(nx - R)
                )
                for dx in -R:R, dy in -R:R
            )
            best = argmax(scores)
            return (name = name, best = best, ratio = scores[(0, 0)] / scores[best])
        end
        out = [reg_offset("axial", recon_HU, gt_resampled_nn)]
        sim_helical === nothing ||
            push!(out, reg_offset("helical", recon_HU_helical, gt_helical_nn))
        out
    end;

        checks = NamedTuple[]
        addcheck(name, value, lo, hi) = push!(
            checks,
            (name = name, value = value, lo = lo, hi = hi, pass = lo <= value <= hi),
        )
        for a in affine_audit
            addcheck(
                "$(a.name): affine vs back-projector grid (µm)",
                a.grid_um,
                0.0,
                1.0e-3,
            )
            addcheck("$(a.name): round trip A⁻¹·A·v − v (voxels)", a.roundtrip, 0.0, 1.0e-9)
        end
        for r in registration
            addcheck(
                "$(r.name): best in-plane shift (pixels, largest component)",
                maximum(abs, r.best),
                0,
                0,
            )
        end
        checks
    end;

Summary

  • Crop the phantom, not the reconstruction. The cardiac block is 17.4 % of the 800 × 700 × 433 phantom; only it was ray-traced, centred on the isocentre where the reconstruction grid always sits.

  • Two affines and one resampler. phantom_to_world_affine and recon_to_world_affine map each grid to world centimetres; resample_to_recon composes them (:nearest for labels, :linear for fields and coverage fractions), and inv(A_phantom) * A_recon hands the map to any other interpolator.

  • Exact, axial and helical. The affine matches the back-projectors' grid to 8.9e-12 µm, the round trip is the identity to 0.0 voxels, and the best image-to-label shift is axial (0, 0), helical (0, 0). Verification: 6 of 6 checks pass.

  • What it buys you. Organ ROIs are one indexing expression: 16 of the 18 labels measured on Scan A's central slice read within 50 HU of their monoenergetic theory. Scan A delivered 17.15 mGy CTDIvol, Scan B 17.14 mGy over 8.0 cm.
